title: Magadha - Shaishunaga dynasty
capsule: The Shaishunaga dynasty ruled the Magadha kingdom in the middle Gangetic plain, traditionally founded by Shishunaga around 413 BC after deposing the Haryanka line, with its capital initially at Rajagriha and later at Pataliputra (Patna). The dynasty's most significant achievement was the destruction of the Pradyota dynasty of Avanti, absorbing that powerful rival kingdom and consolidating Magadha's dominance across north India. The line ended around 345 BC when Mahapadma Nanda, founder of the Nanda dynasty, replaced the last Shaishunaga ruler, continuing Magadha's trajectory toward the pan-Indian empire eventually seized by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BC.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Shaishunaga period is poorly documented; territorial extent is inferred from Puranic king lists, Buddhist chronicles (Mahavamsa, Dipavamsa), and later Magadhan records rather than contemporary inscriptions, making boundaries highly conjectural.
